from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence

class ReviewStrokeKind(enum.Enum):
    """What a stroke is: freehand ink along its points, a shape between them,
    or text at one of them.
    """
    Freehand = 0

    Line = 1

    Arrow = 2

    Rectangle = 3

    Ellipse = 4

    Text = 5

class ReviewStroke:
    """A single stroke of an annotation: freehand ink, a shape, or text.

    The points and the width are expressed in the pixels of the source image,
    so a stroke keeps its position and its weight whatever the zoom, the pan or
    the comparison mode. Both are written with the space they are expressed in,
    and a stroke in a space this version does not know is skipped rather than
    misplaced. See docs/review-format.md.

    What the points are depends on the kind: the path of freehand ink; the two
    ends of a line or an arrow, the head at the second; two opposite corners of
    a rectangle or of the box an ellipse fills; the top left of text. A stroke
    of a kind other than freehand makes the document version 2; see
    reviewVersionFor().
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def kind(self) -> ReviewStrokeKind:
        """What the stroke is."""

    @kind.setter
    def kind(self, arg: ReviewStrokeKind, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def color(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """The color, orange by default."""

    @color.setter
    def color(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def width(self) -> float:
        """The width of the line, in the pixels of the source image."""

    @width.setter
    def width(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def points(self) -> list[feather_tk._feather_tk.V2F]:
        """The points, in the pixels of the source image."""

    @points.setter
    def points(self, arg: Sequence[feather_tk._feather_tk.V2F], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        """The text, for a text stroke, and its height in the pixels of the
        source image.
        """

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def textSize(self) -> float:
        """The height of the text, in the pixels of the source image."""

    @textSize.setter
    def textSize(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def textBackground(self) -> bool:
        """Whether text is drawn on a plate, dark behind light text and light
        behind dark, so it reads over any picture. A reader that does not know
        it draws the text alone.
        """

    @textBackground.setter
    def textBackground(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ReviewStroke, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ReviewStroke, /) -> bool: ...

class ReviewAnnotation:
    """The drawing on one frame of one source."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def id(self) -> str:
        """The annotation's identifier."""

    @id.setter
    def id(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def sourceId(self) -> str:
        """The source the drawing belongs to, by ReviewFile::id."""

    @sourceId.setter
    def sourceId(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def time(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None:
        """The frame the drawing appears on. A drawing is visible on this frame
        only.
        """

    @time.setter
    def time(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def author(self) -> str:
        """Who drew it, and when, ISO 8601. Both are optional: a document
        written before they existed simply leaves them empty.
        """

    @author.setter
    def author(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def created(self) -> str:
        """When it was drawn, ISO 8601."""

    @created.setter
    def created(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def strokes(self) -> list[ReviewStroke]:
        """The strokes, in the order they were drawn."""

    @strokes.setter
    def strokes(self, arg: Sequence[ReviewStroke], /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ReviewAnnotation, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ReviewAnnotation, /) -> bool: ...

class AnnotationsModel:
    """The drawing annotations of a review.

    Adding and erasing strokes go through a command stack, so they can be
    undone and redone. Annotations are session state: they live in the review
    file, not in the application settings.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    @property
    def annotations(self) -> list[ReviewAnnotation]:
        """Get the annotations."""

    @property
    def observeAnnotations(self) -> IObservableReviewAnnotationList:
        """Observe the annotations."""

    def getStrokes(self, sourceId: str, time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime) -> list[ReviewStroke]:
        """Get the strokes drawn on the given source and frame, or an empty
        list if there are none.
        """

    def setAnnotations(self, annotations: Sequence[ReviewAnnotation]) -> None:
        """Replace all the annotations, e.g. when a review is opened. This
        clears the undo history.
        """

    def addStroke(self, sourceId: str, time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, stroke: ReviewStroke) -> None:
        """Add a stroke to the given source and frame."""

    def eraseStrokes(self, sourceId: str, time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, pos: feather_tk._feather_tk.V2F, radius: float) -> None:
        """Erase the strokes of the given source and frame whose path passes
        within the radius of the position. The position and the radius are in
        the pixels of the source image, and text covers what textBox() has it
        cover in the view.
        """

    def clearFrame(self, sourceIds: Sequence[str], time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime) -> None:
        """Remove every stroke of the given sources and frame. One call for all
        of the sources, so that clearing a compared frame is a single undo
        step.
        """

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Remove all the annotations, clearing the undo history."""

    @property
    def observeHasUndo(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether there is a change to undo."""

    @property
    def observeHasRedo(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether there is an undone change to redo."""

    def undo(self) -> None:
        """Undo the last change to the annotations."""

    def redo(self) -> None:
        """Redo the last change undone."""

class ExportStatus(enum.Enum):
    """What an export is doing."""
    Queued = 0

    Running = 1

    Finished = 2

    Failed = 3

    Cancelled = 4

class ExportProgress:
    """How far an export has got."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def status(self) -> ExportStatus:
        """What the export is doing."""

    @status.setter
    def status(self, arg: ExportStatus, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def framesDone(self) -> int:
        """The number of frames written so far."""

    @framesDone.setter
    def framesDone(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property

        """The number of frames to write."""

    @frames.setter
    def frames(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def timeLeft(self) -> str:
        """"about 2 minutes left", once there is enough to go on; see
        getExportTimeLeft().
        """

    @timeLeft.setter
    def timeLeft(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seconds(self) -> float:
        """How long it ran, once it has stopped."""

    @seconds.setter
    def seconds(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def error(self) -> str:
        """Why the export failed."""

    @error.setter
    def error(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

def getTotalLabel(progress: Sequence[ExportProgress]) -> str:
    """The time the finished exports took, added up: "3 done, 6 min 02 s in
    all". Empty with fewer than two, whose own rows say it. Failed and
    cancelled exports are not counted (#976).
    """

class ExportJob:
    """One export. The frames are asked for and rendered on the thread the
    queue runs on, which has the graphics context, a few ahead so that reading,
    rendering and writing overlap; they are written on a thread of the export's
    own, so that an encoder slower than the frames arrive does not hold up the
    application.
    """
    @property
    def name(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def path(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def progress(self) -> ExportProgress:
        """Get how far the export has got."""

class ExportQueue:
    """The exports, run one at a time in the order they were asked for. One at
    a time is the point: each encoder has memory of its own, gigabytes for a
    long GOP codec at 4K.
    """
    @property
    def jobs(self) -> list[ExportJob]:
        """Observe the exports, in the order they run."""

    @property
    def busy(self) -> bool:
        """Observe whether any export is queued or running."""

    def cancel(self, job: ExportJob) -> None:
        """Cancel an export, queued or running."""

    def cancelAll(self) -> None:
        """Cancel every export."""

    def remove(self, job: ExportJob) -> None:
        """Remove an export that has stopped from the list."""

    def clearDone(self) -> None:
        """Remove every export that has stopped."""

class AppInfoModel:
    """Application information model."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    def getFullName(self) -> str:
        """Get the application's name, "DJV", or the one an application built
        on DJV gives.
        """

    def getShortName(self) -> str:
        """Get the application's short name, in lower case: "djv"."""

    def getDocsDirName(self) -> str:
        """Get the name of the directory, under the user's application support
        directory, where the settings and log file are kept. Defaults to the
        full name; a suite of applications built on DJV overrides it so that
        they share one directory instead of scattering one apiece.
        """

    def getTitle(self) -> str:
        """Get the window title: the name and the version, and for a
        development build the commit date and hash as well, so that two of them
        can be told apart. A release is identified by its version, and the rest
        would be noise.
        """

    def getStudioURL(self) -> str:
        """Get the web site for DJV Studio, the commercial version. A brief
        mention with this link appears in the setup dialog and the Help menu;
        returning an empty string hides it, which is what the commercial
        applications themselves do.
        """

    def getDocsSearchPath(self) -> str:
        """Get the directory the documentation search starts from: the
        executable's own, unless an application says otherwise. The Python
        application does -- its executable is the interpreter, which lives
        nowhere near the install.
        """

    @property
    def fullName(self) -> str:
        """Get the application's name, "DJV", or the one an application built
        on DJV gives.
        """

    @property
    def shortName(self) -> str:
        """Get the application's short name, in lower case: "djv"."""

    @property
    def docsDirName(self) -> str:
        """Get the name of the directory, under the user's application support
        directory, where the settings and log file are kept. Defaults to the
        full name; a suite of applications built on DJV overrides it so that
        they share one directory instead of scattering one apiece.
        """

    @property
    def versionMajor(self) -> int:
        """Get the major version number."""

    @property
    def versionMinor(self) -> int:
        """Get the minor version number."""

    @property
    def versionPatch(self) -> int:
        """Get the patch version number."""

    @property
    def versionDev(self) -> str:
        """Get the development suffix: "-dev" for a development version, empty
        for a release.
        """

    @property
    def version(self) -> str:
        """Get the version: the major, minor and patch numbers and the
        development suffix, such as "3.8.0-dev".
        """

    @property
    def commitDate(self) -> str:
        """Get the date of the commit the build was made from."""

    @property
    def gitCommit(self) -> str:
        """Get the commit the build was made from, marked "-dirty" when
        anything was uncommitted.
        """

    @property
    def title(self) -> str:
        """Get the window title: the name and the version, and for a
        development build the commit date and hash as well, so that two of them
        can be told apart. A release is identified by its version, and the rest
        would be noise.
        """

    @property
    def docsURL(self) -> str:
        """Get the documentation installed beside the application, as a file
        URL, or empty when there is none.

        Installed rather than on the web, so that what it describes is the
        version that is running. A build that was not installed -- a
        developer's -- has none, and the menu item says so rather than opening
        nothing.
        """

    @property
    def docsSearchPath(self) -> str:
        """Get the directory the documentation search starts from: the
        executable's own, unless an application says otherwise. The Python
        application does -- its executable is the interpreter, which lives
        nowhere near the install.
        """

    @property
    def license(self) -> str:
        """Get the application's license text."""

    @property
    def licensesURL(self) -> str:
        """Get the licenses page installed beside the application, as a file
        URL, or empty when there is none.

        The notices ship with the build they describe, the way the
        documentation does, so what is listed is what is installed. A link to a
        repository is a list of what some other build carries, which for an
        application built on this library is the wrong list entirely.
        """

    @property
    def studioURL(self) -> str:
        """Get the web site for DJV Studio, the commercial version. A brief
        mention with this link appears in the setup dialog and the Help menu;
        returning an empty string hides it, which is what the commercial
        applications themselves do.
        """

class ColorModel:
    """Color model."""
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, settings: feather_tk._feather_tk.Settings) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    def save(self) -> None:
        """Save the settings."""

    @property
    def ocioOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.OCIOOptions:
        """Get the OpenColorIO options."""

    @ocioOptions.setter
    def ocioOptions(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.OCIOOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeOCIOOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.IObservableOCIOOptions:
        """Observe the OpenColorIO options."""

    @property
    def observeResolvedOCIOOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.IObservableOCIOOptions:
        """Observe the OpenColorIO options with the input color space resolved
        for the active file. This is what rendering should use;
        observeOCIOOptions() is the settings as the user wrote them.
        """

    def setActiveFiles(self, arg: Sequence[tuple[str, Mapping[str, str]]], /) -> None:
        """Set the files that input color spaces are resolved for -- the active
        file first, then the compare files -- with the metadata tags each was
        read with.
        """

    def resolveInput(self, path: str, tags: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> str:
        """Resolve an input color space for a file: the extension assignments,
        then what the file declares, then the configuration's file rules. Empty
        when nothing resolves.
        """

    @property
    def observeResolvedInputs(self) -> IObservableStringVector:
        """Observe the input color space resolved for each of the active files,
        in their order; empty entries resolve nothing and use the options'
        input. For the per item display options overrides.
        """

    @property
    def observeResolvedInput(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableString:
        """Observe the resolved input color space and where it came from, for
        display; e.g., "sRGB (extension)". Empty when nothing is resolved.
        """

    @property
    def extColorSpaces(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Get the file name extension color spaces."""

    @extColorSpaces.setter
    def extColorSpaces(self, arg: Mapping[str, str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeExtColorSpaces(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableStringMap:
        """Observe the file name extension color spaces."""

    @property
    def lutOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.LUTOptions:
        """Get the LUT options."""

    @lutOptions.setter
    def lutOptions(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.LUTOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeLUTOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.IObservableLUTOptions:
        """Observe the LUT options."""

class CommandInfo:
    """Command information."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

        """The command's name, the group and the action: "Timeline/DetectCuts".
        """

    @name.setter

class CommandsModel:
    """Commands model.

    Commands are named, scriptable operations that manipulate the application.
    Menu actions, keyboard shortcuts, and automation (e.g., screenshot capture)
    share this single entry point for invoking application functionality.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    def add(self, name: str, doc: str, func: Callable[[str], None]) -> None:
        """Add a command."""

    def remove(self, name: str) -> None:
        """Remove a command."""

    @property
    def commands(self) -> list[CommandInfo]:
        """Get information about the commands, sorted by name."""

    def exec(self, name: str, args: str = 'null') -> bool:
        """Execute a command. Errors are logged and false is returned."""

class DrawTool(enum.Enum):
    """Drawing tools."""
    Pen = 0

    Eraser = 1

    Line = 2

    Arrow = 3

    Rectangle = 4

    Ellipse = 5

    Text = 6

    Select = 7

def getStrokeKind(tool: DrawTool) -> ReviewStrokeKind:
    """The kind of stroke a tool makes. The eraser and the select tool make
    none and give freehand.
    """

class DrawToolObserver:

class ObservableColor4F(IObservableColor4F):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """Get the value."""

class DrawModel:
    """The drawing state: whether drawing is active, and with what.

    These are preferences rather than review contents, so they are kept in the
    settings and not in the review file.
    """
    def __init__(self, settings: feather_tk._feather_tk.Settings) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Is drawing active? While it is, the viewport draws instead of
        shuttling frames with the left mouse button.
        """

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeEnabled(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether drawing is active."""

    @property
    def tool(self) -> DrawTool:
        """The current tool."""

    @tool.setter
    def tool(self, arg: DrawTool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeTool(self) -> IObservableDrawTool:
        """Observe the current tool."""

    @property
    def color(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """The stroke colour."""

    @color.setter
    def color(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeColor(self) -> IObservableColor4F:
        """Observe the stroke color."""

    @property
    def size(self) -> float:
        """The stroke width, on an HD picture; pictureDrawSize() gives it in
        the pixels of the picture drawn on.
        """

    @size.setter
    def size(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeSize(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableFloat:
        """Observe the stroke width."""

    @property
    def textSize(self) -> float:
        """The height of text, on an HD picture, as the width is."""

    @textSize.setter
    def textSize(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeTextSize(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableFloat:
        """Observe the height of text."""

    @property
    def onionSkin(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the drawings on the frames before and after are shown,
        faded, behind this frame's: where the last frame's note was is what a
        note about motion is drawn against.
        """

    @onionSkin.setter
    def onionSkin(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeOnionSkin(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether the drawings on the frames before and after are
        shown.
        """

    @property
    def constrain(self) -> bool:
        """Whether a shape is held square or round, and a line or an arrow to a
        multiple of forty-five degrees, as Shift holds it: for a touch screen,
        which has no Shift to hold.
        """

    @constrain.setter
    def constrain(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeConstrain(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether shapes and lines are constrained."""

    @property
    def textBackground(self) -> bool:
        """Whether new text is drawn on a background plate, so it reads over
        any picture. On by default.
        """

    @textBackground.setter
    def textBackground(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeTextBackground(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether new text is drawn on a background plate."""

class FilesModelItem:
    """Files model item."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def id(self) -> str:
        """Stable, unique identifier. Assigned when the file is opened so that
        reviews and annotations can reference the file by identity rather than
        by list index. See models::generateId().
        """

    @id.setter
    def id(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def path(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Path:
        """The file's path."""

    @path.setter
    def path(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioPath(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Path:
        """A separate audio file played with it, as File > Open With Audio
        opens one; empty for none.
        """

    @audioPath.setter
    def audioPath(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def videoLayers(self) -> list[str]:
        """The names of the file's video layers, filled in when it is opened.
        """

    @videoLayers.setter
    def videoLayers(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def videoLayer(self) -> int:
        """The video layer shown, an index into the layers."""

    @videoLayer.setter
    def videoLayer(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def mediaReferenceKeys(self) -> list[str]:
        """The media reference keys the file's clips use, from an OTIO timeline
        whose clips carry several versions of their media (e.g., "Full" and
        "Proxy"). Filled in when the file is opened.
        """

    @mediaReferenceKeys.setter
    def mediaReferenceKeys(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def mediaReferenceKey(self) -> str:
        """The media reference key the file is read with. Empty, the default,
        leaves each clip on the reference it was authored with.
        """

    @mediaReferenceKey.setter
    def mediaReferenceKey(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def mediaReferenceKeysKnown(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the keys above are known, which is once the file has been
        opened. Until then a key cannot be checked.
        """

    @mediaReferenceKeysKnown.setter
    def mediaReferenceKeysKnown(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioChannel(self) -> int:
        """The audio channel to play, or -1 for all of the channels."""

    @audioChannel.setter
    def audioChannel(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def speed(self) -> float:
        """The playback speed, in frames per second, when the file last lost
        focus. Negative until then, and the file plays at its own speed.
        """

    @speed.setter
    def speed(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def currentTime(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None:
        """Where playback had got to, and the in/out points, when the file last
        lost focus. Unset until it has been played.
        """

    @currentTime.setter
    def currentTime(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def inOutRange(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None:
        """The in/out points, kept the same way as the current time."""

    @inOutRange.setter
    def inOutRange(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def timeRange(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None:
        """The range the file turned out to have when it was opened. For an
        image sequence this is the frames that were found, which the path does
        not carry when it names a single file. Unset until the file has been
        opened.
        """

    @timeRange.setter
    def timeRange(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def framesStated(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the range on the path was asked for rather than found. A
        stated range is used as it is; an unstated one is looked for on disk
        each time the file is opened, so that frames rendered since last time
        are picked up.
        """

    @framesStated.setter
    def framesStated(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def newFile(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the file has just been opened and not yet been the current
        file. Playback starts on a new file when the playback settings say so.
        """

    @newFile.setter
    def newFile(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class FilesModelItemObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableFilesModelItem, callback: Callable[[FilesModelItem], None], action: feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction = feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

        """Get the value."""

    """Base class for observable lists."""
    pass

class ObservableFilesModelItemList(IObservableFilesModelItemList):
    """Observable list."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[FilesModelItem], /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: Sequence[FilesModelItem], /) -> None:
        """Set the list."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: Sequence[FilesModelItem], /) -> bool:
        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: FilesModelItem) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: FilesModelItem) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: FilesModelItem, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[FilesModelItem], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: FilesModelItem) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[FilesModelItem]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[FilesModelItem]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[FilesModelItem]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> FilesModelItem:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: FilesModelItem, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: FilesModelItem, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

class FilesModel:
    """Files model: the open files, the "A" file, which is the current one, and
    the "B" files it is compared with.
    """
    def __init__(self, settings: feather_tk._feather_tk.Settings) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    def save(self) -> None:
        """Save the settings."""

    @property
    def files(self) -> list[FilesModelItem]:
        """Get the files."""

    @property
    def observeFiles(self) -> IObservableFilesModelItemList:
        """Observe the files."""

    @property
    def a(self) -> FilesModelItem:
        """Get the "A" file."""

    @property
    def observeA(self) -> IObservableFilesModelItem:
        """Observe the "A" file."""

    @property
    def aIndex(self) -> int:
        """Get the "A" file index."""

    @property
    def observeAIndex(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableInt:
        """Observe the "A" file index."""

    @property
    def b(self) -> list[FilesModelItem]:
        """Get the "B" files."""

    @property
    def observeB(self) -> IObservableFilesModelItemList:
        """Observe the "B" files."""

    @property
    def bIndexes(self) -> list[int]:
        """Get the "B" file indexes."""

    @property
    def observeBIndexes(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableIntList:
        """Observe the "B" file indexes."""

    @property
    def active(self) -> list[FilesModelItem]:
        """Get the active files. The active files are the "A" file and "B"
        files.
        """

    @property
    def observeActive(self) -> IObservableFilesModelItemList:
        """Observe the active files. The active files are the "A" file and "B"
        files.
        """

    @overload
    def add(self, arg: FilesModelItem, /) -> None:
        """Add a file.

        Add files together, with the "A" file changing once at the end. Adding
        a list one file at a time would make each of them "A" along the way,
        and everything watching would open each of them along the way too.
        """

    @overload
    def add(self, arg: Sequence[FilesModelItem], /) -> None:
        """Add a file.

        Add files together, with the "A" file changing once at the end. Adding
        a list one file at a time would make each of them "A" along the way,
        and everything watching would open each of them along the way too.
        """

    def move(self, fromIndex: int, toIndex: int) -> None:
        """Move a file so it ends at the given index. The "A" and "B" choices
        follow the file: reordering changes where things are, not what is being
        looked at.
        """

    @overload
    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the current "A" file.

        Close the given file.
        """

    @overload
    def close(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Close the current "A" file.

        Close the given file.
        """

    def closeAll(self) -> None:
        """Close all the files."""

    def setA(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Set the "A" file."""

    def setB(self, index: int, value: bool) -> None:
        """Set the "B" files."""

    def toggleB(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Toggle a "B" file."""

    def clearB(self) -> None:
        """Clear the "B" files."""

    def first(self) -> None:
        """Set the "A" file to the first file."""

    def last(self) -> None:
        """Set the "A" file to the last file."""

    def next(self) -> None:
        """Set the "A" file to the next file."""

    def prev(self) -> None:
        """Set the "A" file to the previous file."""

    def firstB(self) -> None:
        """Set the "B" file to the first file."""

    def lastB(self) -> None:
        """Set the "B" file to the last file."""

    def nextB(self) -> None:
        """Set the "B" file to the next file."""

    def prevB(self) -> None:
        """Set the "B" file to the previous file."""

    @property
    def observeLayers(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableIntList:
        """Observe the layers."""

    def setLayer(self, item: FilesModelItem, layer: int) -> None:
        """Set a layer."""

    @property
    def observeMediaReferenceKeys(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableStringList:
        """Observe the media reference key of each file, in order."""

    def setMediaReferenceKey(self, item: FilesModelItem, key: str) -> None:
        """Set a file's media reference key; empty for the references the clips
        were authored with. A key the file does not use is ignored. A file that
        has not been opened yet has no keys to check against, so any key is
        taken, and checked when it opens (see
        FilesModelItem::mediaReferenceKeysKnown).
        """

    def nextMediaReferenceKey(self) -> None:
        """Set the "A" file to its next media reference key. The empty key is
        not part of the cycle; it is chosen from the menu.
        """

    def setFrames(self, item: FilesModelItem, range: feather_tk._feather_tk.RangeI64) -> None:
        """Set the frame range of an image sequence. This is the range the
        sequence is meant to cover, which need not be the frames that are on
        disk: a render in progress is watched over the range it will have when
        it finishes. The file is reopened, since everything about a timeline is
        derived from its path.
        """

    @property
    def observeReload(self) -> IObservableFilesModelItem:
        """Observe files that have to be reopened."""

    def refresh(self) -> None:
        """Announce the files again, for a change to what an item holds rather
        than to which items there are. The items are shared and written to in
        place -- the frame range and the layers are filled in once the file has
        been opened -- and the list itself does not change when they are, so
        nothing else says so.

        The "A" file is announced again too, for the observers that take it
        directly rather than through the list.
        """

    def nextLayer(self) -> None:
        """Set the "A" file to the next layer."""

    def prevLayer(self) -> None:
        """Set the "A" file to the previous layer."""

    @property
    def audioChannel(self) -> int:
        """Get the "A" file's audio channel, or -1 for all of the channels."""

    @property
    def observeAudioChannel(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableInt:
        """Observe the "A" file's audio channel."""

    def setAudioChannel(self, item: FilesModelItem, channel: int) -> None:
        """Set a file's audio channel, or -1 for all of the channels."""

    @property
    def compareOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.CompareOptions:
        """Get the compare options."""

    @compareOptions.setter
    def compareOptions(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.CompareOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCompareOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.IObservableCompareOptions:
        """Observe the compare options."""

    @property
    def compareTime(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.CompareTime:
        """Get the compare time mode."""

    @compareTime.setter
    def compareTime(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.CompareTime, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCompareTime(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.IObservableCompareTime:
        """Observe the compare time mode."""

    @property
    def wipeHandles(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the wipe's handles are shown over the picture: the dot that
        moves it and the ring that turns it. Hidden, the wipe is moved with the
        mouse binding and the Files tool.
        """

    @wipeHandles.setter
    def wipeHandles(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeWipeHandles(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether the wipe's handles are shown."""

def getCompareTimeLabels() -> list[str]:
    """Labels for the comparison time, as shown to the user. The enumeration's
    own labels name the setting where it is stored and in the keyboard
    shortcuts, so they say what the values are rather than what they do, and
    are not these.
    """

def reviewMarkerColor() -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
    """The default marker color."""

class ReviewMarker:
    """Review feedback: a marker anchored to a span of frames.

    One type covers what used to be two: a note is a marker with text and a
    one-frame span, a named range is a marker with a name and a wider one, and
    a marker may be both. The fields map one to one onto OTIO markers, so
    import and export are lossless by construction. Markers belong to the
    review rather than to a source: the frames locate them. See
    docs/review-format.md.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def id(self) -> str:
        """The marker's identifier."""

    @id.setter
    def id(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Short label. Optional: the interface shows the frames when there is
        no name to show.
        """

    @name.setter
    def name(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def range(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None:
        """The frames the marker is about; a single frame is a one-frame span.
        Optional: a marker about no frame in particular speaks about the whole
        review.
        """

    @range.setter
    def range(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def color(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """The color, green by default."""

    @color.setter
    def color(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        """The body."""

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def author(self) -> str:
        """Who wrote it. Optional: empty when the environment does not say."""

    @author.setter
    def author(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def created(self) -> str:
        """When the marker was made, ISO 8601."""

    @created.setter
    def created(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ReviewMarker, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ReviewMarker, /) -> bool: ...

class ReviewMarkerListObserver:
    """List observer."""
    def __init__(self, observableList: IObservableReviewMarkerList, callback: Callable[[Sequence[ReviewMarker]], None], action: feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction = feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

    """Base class for observable lists."""
    pass

        """Set the list."""

        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: ReviewMarker) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: ReviewMarker) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: ReviewMarker, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[ReviewMarker], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: ReviewMarker) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[ReviewMarker]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[ReviewMarker]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[ReviewMarker]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> ReviewMarker:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: ReviewMarker, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: ReviewMarker, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

class MarkersModel:
    """The review markers.

    Markers are session state: they live in the review file, not in the
    application settings. The list is kept in time order with the markers about
    no frame in particular first, so every reader shows the same feedback in
    the same order.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    @property
    def markers(self) -> list[ReviewMarker]:
        """Get the markers."""

    @property
    def observeMarkers(self) -> IObservableReviewMarkerList:
        """Observe the markers."""

    def setMarkers(self, markers: Sequence[ReviewMarker]) -> None:
        """Replace all the markers, e.g. when a review is opened."""

    def add(self, range: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None, name: str, text: str) -> str:
        """Add a marker, returning its identifier. The identifier, creation
        time and author are filled in here, so callers only provide the rest.
        """

    def update(self, id: str, text: str) -> None:
        """Replace the text of the marker with the given identifier. The
        creation time and author stay: they say who raised the point and when,
        not who last touched the wording.
        """

    def updateColor(self, id: str, color: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F) -> None:
        """Replace the color of the marker with the given identifier."""

    def remove(self, id: str) -> None:
        """Remove the marker with the given identifier."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Remove all the markers."""

class OCIOModelData:
    """OpenColorIO model data."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether OpenColorIO is enabled."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def config(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.OCIOConfig:
        """Which configuration is used."""

    @config.setter
    def config(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.OCIOConfig, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fileName(self) -> str:
        """The configuration file, for File."""

    @fileName.setter
    def fileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The configuration's name, or where it has none the file's, or for a
        "config.ocio" its directory's.
        """

    @name.setter
    def name(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def inputs(self) -> list[str]:
        """The input color spaces. The first is "Automatic", which resolves
        each file's from the extension assignments, what the file declares, and
        the configuration's file rules.
        """

    @inputs.setter
    def inputs(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def inputIndex(self) -> int:
        """The input color space in use, an index into the inputs."""

    @inputIndex.setter
    def inputIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def displays(self) -> list[str]:
        """The configuration's displays."""

    @displays.setter
    def displays(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def displayIndex(self) -> int:
        """The display in use, an index into the displays."""

    @displayIndex.setter
    def displayIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def views(self) -> list[str]:
        """The views of the display in use."""

    @views.setter
    def views(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def viewIndex(self) -> int:
        """The view in use, an index into the views."""

    @viewIndex.setter
    def viewIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def looks(self) -> list[str]:
        """The configuration's looks. The first is "None"."""

    @looks.setter
    def looks(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def lookIndex(self) -> int:
        """The look in use, an index into the looks."""

    @lookIndex.setter
    def lookIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: OCIOModelData, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: OCIOModelData, /) -> bool: ...

class OCIOModelDataObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableOCIOModelData, callback: Callable[[OCIOModelData], None], action: feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction = feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableOCIOModelData:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> OCIOModelData:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableOCIOModelData(IObservableOCIOModelData):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: OCIOModelData, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: OCIOModelData, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: OCIOModelData, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> OCIOModelData:
        """Get the value."""

class OCIOModel:
    """OpenColorIO model: a configuration's color spaces, displays, views and
    looks, and the options chosen from them. The application's color options
    are the color model's; a color widget keeps a model of its own in step with
    them.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    def setOptions(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.OCIOOptions, /) -> None:
        """Set the options."""

    @property
    def observeOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.IObservableOCIOOptions:
        """Observe the options."""

    @property
    def observeData(self) -> IObservableOCIOModelData:
        """Observe the model data."""

    def setEnabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None:
        """Set whether the color configuration is enabled."""

    def setConfig(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.OCIOConfig, /) -> None:
        """Set the color configuration."""

    def setFileName(self, fileName: str) -> None:
        """Set the color configuration file."""

    def setInputIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None:
        """Set the input index."""

    def setDisplayIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None:
        """Set the display index."""

    def setViewIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None:
        """Set the view index."""

    def setLookIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None:
        """Set the look index."""

def parseFrameRange(value: str) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.RangeI64:
    """Parse a frame range such as "1-100", and "-10-20" for a sequence
    starting before zero: the separator is the first dash after the first
    character, so a negative start is not mistaken for it. Throws on anything
    else.
    """

def parseTime(name: str, value: str, speed: float, units: tlrender._tlrender.TimeUnits) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime:
    """Parse a time in the given units. The name is for the error message ("in
    point", "seek time"), which is thrown.
    """

class Playlist:
    """A playlist: the open file list and the compare state, as saved to and
    opened from an ".otio" file.

    A playlist is deliberately not a session. What belongs here is what stops
    making sense when the set of open files changes -- the order, the per-file
    state, and the A/B comparison. Color, view, and window state stay in the
    settings.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def items(self) -> list[FilesModelItem]:
        """The files, in order."""

    @items.setter
    def items(self, arg: Sequence[FilesModelItem], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def aIndex(self) -> int:
        """The "A" file, an index into the items; -1 for none."""

    @aIndex.setter
    def aIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def bIndexes(self) -> list[int]:
        """The "B" files, as indexes into the items."""

    @bIndexes.setter
    def bIndexes(self, arg: Sequence[int], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def compareOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.CompareOptions:
        """The compare options."""

    @compareOptions.setter
    def compareOptions(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.CompareOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def compareTime(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.CompareTime:
        """The compare time mode."""

    @compareTime.setter
    def compareTime(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.CompareTime, /) -> None: ...

def playlistSave(fileName: str, playlist: Playlist, defaultRate: float = 24.0) -> None:
    """Save a playlist to an ".otio" file."""

def playlistApply(playlist: Playlist, filesModel: FilesModel) -> None:
    """Open a playlist's files in the file list, after what is already open,
    with its "A" and "B" files and its compare state.

    The comparison replaces the one in the file list, and is rebuilt in the
    order the review does it: the compare state first, since in a mode that
    shows one "B" file each new "B" replaces the last -- a tiled comparison set
    before its mode came back as one "B" -- then the "B" files, cleared first
    of the one the mode picks for itself, then the "A" file.
    """

def playlistOpen(fileName: str) -> tuple:
    """Open a playlist from an ".otio" file.

    Throws on a file that cannot be read, and on a playlist written by a newer
    DJV, since silently dropping what the newer version wrote would corrupt it
    on the next save.
    """

class RecentFilesModel(feather_tk._feather_tk.RecentFilesModel):
    """Recent files model."""
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, settings: feather_tk._feather_tk.Settings, settingsGroup: str = 'Files', recentMax: int = 10) -> None:
        """Create a new model; "recentMax" is how many are kept unless another
        number was saved. The settings group is the prefix under which the
        recent list is persisted, e.g. "Files" -> "/Files/Recent".
        """

    def save(self) -> None:
        """Save the settings."""

reviewVersion: int = 2

def reviewVersionSupported(version: int) -> bool:
    """Whether this build can read a review document of the given version.

    False means the document was written by a newer DJV. Reading it anyway
    would drop what this build does not understand, and the next save would
    write that loss back over the user's file.
    """

def reviewVersionFor(review: Review) -> int:
    """The version a review is written as: the lowest one that reads everything
    in it, so that a document stays open to older versions until it holds
    something they would get wrong.
    """

def reviewExtension() -> str:
    """The review file extension (".djvr")."""

def sameTime(arg0: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None, arg1: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None, /) -> bool:
    """Whether two optional times are the same: both unset, or the same value
    at the same rate.
    """

def sameRange(arg0: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None, arg1: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None, /) -> bool:
    """Whether two optional time ranges are the same: both unset, or the same
    start and duration at the same rate.
    """

def generateId() -> str:
    """Generate a stable, unique identifier for a review file entry.

    Assigned when a file is opened so that annotations and notes (phase 3) can
    reference a file by identity rather than by list index, which is not stable
    across close/reorder.
    """

def timestamp() -> str:
    """The current UTC time, ISO 8601 (e.g. "2026-07-26T18:05:00Z")."""

def reviewAuthor() -> str:
    """Who is making the markers and the drawings: the author set with
    setReviewAuthor(), and where none is set the user name the system gives
    (USERNAME on Windows, USER elsewhere), except on the iPad, whose user is
    the same for everyone. DJV has no accounts and reviews are passed from hand
    to hand, so this is a label rather than an identity: it says who wrote a
    note when a session comes back from someone else.
    """

class ReviewFile:
    """A single file entry in a review."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def id(self) -> str:
        """The file's identifier, which the rest of the review refers to it by.
        """

    @id.setter
    def id(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def path(self) -> str:
        """Preferred: relative to the .djvr."""

    @path.setter
    def path(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pathAbsolute(self) -> str:
        """Fallback: absolute path."""

    @pathAbsolute.setter
    def pathAbsolute(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioPath(self) -> str:
        """Separate audio, resolved like the file above: the relative form is
        preferred, the absolute one is the fallback.
        """

    @audioPath.setter
    def audioPath(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioPathAbsolute(self) -> str:
        """The separate audio's absolute path."""

    @audioPathAbsolute.setter
    def audioPathAbsolute(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def videoLayer(self) -> int:
        """The video layer shown, by index."""

    @videoLayer.setter
    def videoLayer(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def speed(self) -> float:
        """The playback speed, in frames per second. Negative is none saved,
        and the file plays at its own speed.
        """

    @speed.setter
    def speed(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def currentTime(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None:
        """The current time. Unset when the file had not been played."""

    @currentTime.setter
    def currentTime(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def inOutRange(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None:
        """The in/out points. Unset when the file had not been played."""

    @inOutRange.setter
    def inOutRange(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None, /) -> None: ...

class ReviewUI:
    """Interface state for a review. The window layout is deliberately absent:
    it belongs to the reader, not the session.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def openTools(self) -> list[str]:
        """The open tool panels, in their listed order."""

    @openTools.setter
    def openTools(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

class Review:
    """A complete review: files, comparison, view, color and interface state.

    Serialized to a versioned JSON document with the ".djvr" extension.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def version(self) -> int:
        """The version the document was read as. It is written as
        reviewVersionFor() says.
        """

    @version.setter
    def version(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def app(self) -> str:
        """The application and version that wrote the document."""

    @app.setter
    def app(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def created(self) -> str:
        """When the document was written, ISO 8601 UTC."""

    @created.setter
    def created(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def files(self) -> list[ReviewFile]:
        """The files, in tab order."""

    @files.setter
    def files(self, arg: Sequence[ReviewFile], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def compare(self) -> ReviewCompare:
        """The A/B comparison: the files, the options and the time mode."""

    @compare.setter
    def compare(self, arg: ReviewCompare, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def view(self) -> ReviewView:
        """The view's framing, pan and zoom."""

    @view.setter
    def view(self, arg: ReviewView, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def color(self) -> ReviewColor:
        """The color and image display options."""

    @color.setter
    def color(self, arg: ReviewColor, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def ui(self) -> ReviewUI:
        """The interface state: the open tools."""

    @ui.setter
    def ui(self, arg: ReviewUI, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def annotations(self) -> list[ReviewAnnotation]:
        """The drawings, by file and frame."""

    @annotations.setter
    def annotations(self, arg: Sequence[ReviewAnnotation], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def markers(self) -> list[ReviewMarker]:
        """The markers."""

    @markers.setter
    def markers(self, arg: Sequence[ReviewMarker], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def unreadSections(self) -> list[str]:
        """The top-level sections that were present but could not be read, by
        name.

        A section is written by a serializer that requires every key it knows,
        so a single key added upstream makes the whole section fail. Letting
        that failure through would cost the user the rest of the document --
        the annotations and the notes above all -- so the section is skipped
        instead, and saving copies it back out of the raw document untouched
        rather than overwriting it with defaults.
        """

    def carryUnread(self, other: Review) -> None: ...

def reviewOpen(fileName: str) -> Review:
    """Open a review from a ".djvr" file.

    Throws on a file that cannot be read, and on a review written by a newer
    DJV, since silently dropping what the newer version wrote would corrupt it
    on the next save. The sections that were present but could not be read are
    in Review::unreadSections.
    """

def reviewSave(fileName: str, review: Review) -> None:
    """Save a review to a ".djvr" file. Throws on a file that cannot be
    written. The document as written becomes Review::raw, so a following save
    carries forward from this one.
    """

def reviewRelativePath(path: str, base: str | os.PathLike) -> str:
    """Make an absolute path string relative to the review's directory, falling
    back to the absolute form when no relative path exists (e.g. a different
    drive on Windows).
    """

def reviewGenericPath(path: str) -> str:
    """Store a path with forward slashes, whatever the platform wrote.

    Windows accepts either separator, so this costs nothing there and keeps a
    document legible -- and diffable -- when it travels.
    """

def resolveReviewPath(relative: str, absolute: str, base: str | os.PathLike, substituteRoot: str | os.PathLike = ..., pathOptions: feather_tk._feather_tk.PathOptions = ...) -> tuple[pathlib.Path, bool]:
    """Resolve a stored relative/absolute path pair to a path on disk,
    preferring the relative form, then the absolute form, then the file's name
    inside an optional substitute root (used by the relocation dialog). Reports
    whether the target exists.
    """

class AudioSettings:
    """Audio settings."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def bufferFrameCount(self) -> int:
        """The size of the buffer the audio device is asked for, in sample
        frames; zero is the device's own default. Larger buffers are less
        likely to underrun and produce glitches; smaller ones reduce latency.
        """

    @bufferFrameCount.setter
    def bufferFrameCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: AudioSettings, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: AudioSettings, /) -> bool: ...

class ExportRenderSize(enum.Enum):
    """Export render size: the source's own, a preset width, a width typed in,
    or a width and height typed in. A width alone has the height follow the
    aspect ratio of what is being exported.
    """
    Source = 0

    Width = 4

    Custom = 5

def getExportRenderSizeEnums() -> list[ExportRenderSize]:
    """Get every value of ExportRenderSize."""

    """Convert to a string."""

    """Convert to a string."""

    """Convert to a string."""

def to_string(arg: TimelineThumbnailSize, /) -> str:
    """Convert to a string."""

@overload
def to_string(arg: HUDItem, /) -> str:
    """Convert to a string."""

@overload
def to_string(arg: HUDPos, /) -> str:
    """Convert to a string."""

@overload
def from_string(arg0: str, arg1: ExportRenderSize, /) -> bool:
    """Convert from a string into the given object, returning whether the
    string names a value. A Python enum cannot be changed in place, so for one
    this only says whether the string is valid.
    """

@overload
def from_string(arg0: str, arg1: ExportFileType, /) -> bool:
    """Convert from a string into the given object, returning whether the
    string names a value. A Python enum cannot be changed in place, so for one
    this only says whether the string is valid.
    """

def getWidth(renderSize: ExportRenderSize) -> int:
    """Get an export render width, or zero for the sizes that are not one of
    the presets.
    """

class ExportFileType(enum.Enum):
    """Export file type."""
    Image = 0

    Seq = 1

    Movie = 2

    """Get every value of ExportFileType."""

class ExportSettings:
    """Export settings."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dir(self) -> str:
        """The directory the exports are written to. One that is empty when the
        settings are read is set to the home directory.
        """

    @dir.setter
    def dir(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def renderSize(self) -> ExportRenderSize:
        """The size the export is rendered at."""

    @renderSize.setter
    def renderSize(self, arg: ExportRenderSize, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def customWidth(self) -> int:
        """The width typed in, for Width and Custom, and the height for Custom,
        used as they are.
        """

    @customWidth.setter
    def customWidth(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def customHeight(self) -> int:
        """The height typed in, for Custom."""

    @customHeight.setter
    def customHeight(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fileType(self) -> ExportFileType:
        """The kind of export, as the tabs of the Export tool choose it."""

    @fileType.setter
    def fileType(self, arg: ExportFileType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def imageFileName(self) -> str:
        """The output file names, without their extensions. A run of '#' is
        where the frame number goes, as many digits wide as there are '#';
        digits are always part of the name.
        """

    @imageFileName.setter
    def imageFileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def imageExt(self) -> str:
        """The extension of an image export, which chooses its file format."""

    @imageExt.setter
    def imageExt(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seqFileName(self) -> str:
        """The name of a sequence export."""

    @seqFileName.setter
    def seqFileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seqExt(self) -> str:
        """The extension of a sequence export, which chooses its file format.
        """

    @seqExt.setter
    def seqExt(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def movieFileName(self) -> str:
        """The name of a movie export."""

    @movieFileName.setter
    def movieFileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def movieExt(self) -> str:
        """The extension of a movie export: one of those the preset writes."""

    @movieExt.setter
    def movieExt(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def moviePreset(self) -> str:
        """The movie export preset. Presets are the whole surface: what they
        cannot express is what tlbake and the command line writer's options are
        for.
        """

    @moviePreset.setter
    def moviePreset(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def movieAudioCodec(self) -> str:
        """The audio codec of a movie export, by its codec name, such as "aac".
        "Auto" leaves it to the file format.
        """

    @movieAudioCodec.setter
    def movieAudioCodec(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ExportSettings, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ExportSettings, /) -> bool: ...

class FileBrowserSettings:
    """File browser settings."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def nativeFileDialog(self) -> bool:
        """Whether files are chosen with the platform's own file dialog rather
        than the built-in file browser. Where the build has no native dialog it
        is kept but does nothing.
        """

    @nativeFileDialog.setter
    def nativeFileDialog(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def path(self) -> str:
        """The directory the built-in file browser is in. It is given to the
        file browser at startup and read back from it when the settings are
        saved, so setting it does not move the file browser.
        """

    @path.setter
    def path(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def options(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.FileBrowserOptions:
        """The built-in file browser's options, kept the same way as the path.
        """

    @options.setter
    def options(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.FileBrowserOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def ext(self) -> str:
        """The extension the built-in file browser filters by, kept the same
        way as the path.
        """

    @ext.setter
    def ext(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: FileBrowserSettings, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: FileBrowserSettings, /) -> bool: ...

class ImageSeqSettings:
    """Image sequence settings."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audio(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.ImageSeqAudio:
        """How an image sequence finds its audio: not at all, by extension, or
        by file name.
        """

    @audio.setter
    def audio(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.ImageSeqAudio, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioExts(self) -> list[str]:
        """The audio file extensions looked for, by extension: first a file
        with the sequence's base name, then the first such file in its
        directory.
        """

    @audioExts.setter
    def audioExts(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioFileName(self) -> str:
        """The audio file opened with a sequence, by file name, in the
        sequence's directory.
        """

    @audioFileName.setter
    def audioFileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def maxDigits(self) -> int:
        """The most digits a frame number can have. A file name ending in more
        is not read as a frame of a sequence.
        """

    @maxDigits.setter
    def maxDigits(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def readThreadCount(self) -> int:
        """How many frames are decoded at once. This is a timeline setting
        rather than a per format one: the timeline is what decodes sequences.
        """

    @readThreadCount.setter
    def readThreadCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def io(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.SeqOptions:
        """The sequence read options: the default speed and what to do about a
        missing frame.
        """

    @io.setter
    def io(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.SeqOptions, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ImageSeqSettings, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ImageSeqSettings, /) -> bool: ...

class OTIOSettings:
    """OTIO settings."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def compat(self) -> bool:
        """Whether to work around timelines that do not conform exactly to the
        specification.

    @compat.setter
    def compat(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: OTIOSettings, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: OTIOSettings, /) -> bool: ...

class MiscSettings:
    """Miscellaneous settings."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def tooltipsEnabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether tooltips are shown. Always off in the tablet build, where
        nothing hovers.
        """

    @tooltipsEnabled.setter
    def tooltipsEnabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def showSetup(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the tour is shown at startup. It is turned off when the tour
        is shown, so a first start shows it once.
        """

    @showSetup.setter
    def showSetup(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def clearRecentOnExit(self) -> bool:
        """Forget the recent files, playlists, reviews and directories when the
        application exits (DJV #909).
        """

    @clearRecentOnExit.setter
    def clearRecentOnExit(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: MiscSettings, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: MiscSettings, /) -> bool: ...

class MouseAction(enum.Enum):
    """Mouse actions."""
    PanView = 0

    CompareWipe = 1

    Pick = 2

    FrameShuttle = 3

def getMouseActionEnums() -> list[MouseAction]:
    """Get every value of MouseAction."""

class MouseActionBinding:
    """Mouse action binding."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, button: feather_tk._feather_tk.MouseButton, modifier: feather_tk._feather_tk.KeyModifier = feather_tk._feather_tk.KeyModifier._None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def button(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.MouseButton:
        """The mouse button."""

    @button.setter
    def button(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.MouseButton, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def modifier(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.KeyModifier:
        """The modifier key held with the button."""

    @modifier.setter
    def modifier(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.KeyModifier, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: MouseActionBinding, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: MouseActionBinding, /) -> bool: ...

class MouseSettings:
    """Mouse settings."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def bindings(self) -> dict[MouseAction, MouseActionBinding]:
        """The mouse button and modifier key bound to each action."""

    @bindings.setter
    def bindings(self, arg: Mapping[MouseAction, MouseActionBinding], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def wheelScale(self) -> float:
        """The factor one click of the mouse wheel zooms the view and the
        timeline by. The Settings tool allows 0.5 to 5.
        """

    @wheelScale.setter
    def wheelScale(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def frameShuttleScale(self) -> float:
        """How fast the frame shuttle steps: at one, a frame each 20 pixels
        dragged. The Settings tool allows 0.1 to 10.
        """

    @frameShuttleScale.setter
    def frameShuttleScale(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: MouseSettings, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: MouseSettings, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: PlaybackSettings, /) -> bool: ...

    Medium = 1

    Large = 2
